description:
FOUND while re-measuring the corpus for the fz-kdt.127.2 fold (F3).

WHAT WAS SEEN. Two full base-vs-head sweeps ran the SAME base binary
(built at 8c3d5ce90, kept at
scratchpad/refute127.2/base-target/release/fz2) over the SAME input
`fixtures2/00277_enum_tier0_fixture.fz` with `interp --dump backend=`, in two
different sessions and two different worktrees of the same commit. They
produced two different backend programs:

  refuter's sweep   md5 cafaf7f634cd1428c3b4c5cd1e6c5e50   3 dispatch nodes, 180 executables
  this sweep        md5 dc9a2fc736688054199696ab555d1164   2 dispatch nodes, 181 executables

571 diff lines: a shifted entry id (x180 vs x179), two `construction=w6`/`w7`
swaps on `Enum.reduce/3#lambda`, a `whole` vs `fields(whole, whole)` transport
demand on two returns, and a callable-resolution set that carries an extra
`Enum.reverse/2#lambda` target per row in the refuter's run.

The HEAD side of both sweeps is byte-identical (a01cd349f960b1346c2a0313e3da4602),
so whatever this is, it did not move with fz-kdt.127.2.

NOT REPRODUCIBLE HERE. The base binary was re-run on the same file 5x
sequentially and 12x in parallel (deliberate contention): all 17 runs produced
dc9a2fc7..., 2 dispatch nodes, 181 executables. The head binary is equally
stable across 17 runs.

WHY IT MATTERS. It is the only thing separating "seven fixtures lose a
dispatch node" (the refuter's count, and what
.agent/docs/semantic-fixpoint.md said before the fold) from "five" (this
sweep's count): 00277 was one of the seven, and in this tree its counts do not
move at all. It is also one of exactly two fixtures whose dump moves when the
agenda is flipped FIFO/LIFO at BOTH base and head (the other is
`dead_closure_capture_empty_list`), and `enum_tier0` is one of the three
known-red `fixture_matrix` lanes. So this fixture is already the corpus's
order-sensitivity hot spot.

WORK: settle whether the discrepancy is (a) real nondeterminism in the
compiler reachable only under some condition not reproduced here, (b) a stale
or dirty tree in the refuter's worktree during its sweep (that worktree has
since been deleted, so it cannot be inspected), or (c) an input difference.
Start by making `00277_enum_tier0_fixture`'s canon a determinism gate under
the same stress lens fz-kdt.127.2 used, and by looking for a non-monotone join
in the transport demand that flips `whole` vs `fields(whole, whole)`.
title: 00277_enum_tier0_fixture compiled to two different backend programs from one binary on one input: cross-session discrepancy, not reproducible in 17 same-session runs
